subject: Life Skills
title: The Ben Franklin Effect
description: A quick, practical guide to The Ben Franklin Effect.

hook.text: Ben Franklin won over a political rival by asking to borrow a rare book. The rival lent it and became his ally.

buildup.text: Asking for a favor makes people like you more, not less. The act of helping creates a psychological bond in the helper.

discovery.text: The Ben Franklin Effect reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Doing favors for someone you dislike also changes your feelings.

climax.text: Ask for small, specific favors. 'Could you recommend a good book?' costs nothing and quietly builds a bridge.

punchline.text: Want them to like you? Let them help you first.

quiz.question: Why does asking for a favor increase likability?
options: People enjoy feeling needed and important
The brain rationalizes 'I helped them, so I must like them'
Small favors create a debt the other person wants to repay
